01-hook: In this town, my family stole things. My dad took a sword once, my sister took a whole cooked chicken, and I was the worst thief we ever had. And every night there were berries on our windowsill. One boy was paying us back for every single thing we took. We never once asked why. Here's how it worked. We carry one thing in our mouth, and if we find food, we drop it to eat. He worked that out. He left food, we left the thing. Then I took a red flower off his windowsill, and that one couldn't be paid for.
02-rule: On my first night alone my dad gave me the rules. "One thing, and nothing anybody is holding." Then I saw the window with a cup on the sill, open a hand's width every night, and in the cup, one red flower. I didn't even have to climb. It was the easiest thing I ever took. Not a sword. A flower, and I thought, this is a thing that matters. I carried it home in my mouth.
03-morning: In the morning I watched the house from the hedge, and the boy came out to the cup, he looked in it, then he sat on the step and cried. The iron golem came up the path and stopped. It gave him that flower. I worked that out later. My sister found me in the hedge with a whole chicken in her mouth. "You took a thing that was a present," she said. "That's not stealing. That's hurting," "take it back in the day. That's the only way it counts."
04-daylight: So I went back in the day, a fox in a village at noon, and every dog in that town knew before I did. I got halfway up the path and the golem turned round, so I ran with the flower still in my mouth. That night there were berries on the sill, a little pile, red, and I dropped the flower, because of course I ate them, that's what a fox does. Then I went home with nothing at all.
05-trade: Next night, more berries than ever. "He's not scared of us," my sister said. "He's waiting." So I looked in our den, behind all of it, berries. One berry under every single thing we ever took. Every one. He counted every one. Then I looked at the cup, and the golem, and the flower, and I got it. That flower wasn't stolen. It was given. So he couldn't buy it back. He was paying us back, one thing a night, and the one thing he wanted was the one thing we never sold. And in the cup that morning, a new flower, and a second cup beside it. Empty.
06-button: So I put a berry in it. I'm a terrible thief. My sister says it's the first thing I ever took worth anything. In this town my family stole things. I traded. Subscribe before I find out what he wants for the sword.
